  - Manufacturing and distribution through over 110 manufacturing and distribution facilities; sales through OEM supply arrangements, retail dealers, wholesale distributors, service centers, and direct-to-consumer online platforms.

     - Description of activities: Supplies components to OEMs in recreation (primarily RV), transportation, and housing markets; strategically located manufacturing and distribution to service OEMs in North America and Europe.

Major OEM customers include Thor Industries, Forest River (Berkshire Hathaway subsidiaries), Winnebago, Brunswick, Polaris, Blue Bird, Skyline Champion, Cavco.
  2) Aftermarket segment
     - Description of activities: Sells discretionary accessories, replacement parts and upgrades for recreation and transportation markets via dealers, distributors, service centers and direct online; includes subsidiary Curt Manufacturing LLC (towing products and truck accessories).

  - Outdoor recreation, transportation, and building products; key industry verticals include recreational vehicles (RVs), marine products, utility trailers, transportation (buses, trucks, trains), and residential and commercial construction (manufactured/modular homes).
- End markets served:
  - RV OEMs and RV owners/aftermarket, marine, automotive, trailer, manufactured housing, commercial transportation.
- Position in the value chain:
  - Manufacturer and supplier of engineered components; supplier/partner to OEMs and provider of aftermarket parts and accessories.

- Primary geographic markets:
  - North America and Europe.
- International operations (if any):

     - Description of activities: Coating third‑party medical devices using hydromer technologies; pilot and production coating capabilities.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Primary / secondary (significant source post‑acquisition of Biosearch Medical Products).
  3) Hydrogels and related product candidates
     - Description of activities: Development of hydrogels for wound care, implants, drug delivery, cosmetics; pilot coating machine to facilitate commercialization; some FDA 510(k) notices for hydrophilic polyurethane foam.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Secondary / emerging (many applications not yet commercialized).

     - Description of activities: Historically provided ISO 13485 / FDA‑registered OEM device manufacturing and private label products; many product lines sold or transitioned.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Minor (company sold most OEM product lines in 2009 and transitioned others in 2010; remaining biofeedback business noted).

     - Description of activities: Prototyping, process development, small/medium scale manufacturing, anti‑microbial testing capability.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Supportive / secondary

====================
STRUCTURED SUMMARY
====================

1. Company Overview
- Legal company name: J J Snack Foods Corp
- Headquarters location: Not stated (incorporated in 1971 under the laws of the State of New Jersey)
- Year founded (if stated): Incorporated 1971
- Public listing / ticker (if stated): Not stated

2. Primary Business Activities
- Core products and/or services:
  - Manufacture and sale of snack foods: soft pretzels, frozen novelties (e.g., Dippin' Dots, Luigi's, Whole Fruit, Dogsters, Philly Swirl, Minute Maid-branded items), churros (Hola, California Churros), bakery products (Readi Bake, Country Home, Mary B's, Daddy Ray's, Hill Valley), funnel cakes, handheld products.
  - Distribution, installation, sales and servicing of frozen beverages and related equipment (Icee, Slush Puppie, Parrot Ice).
  - Private label and contract packing.
  - Equipment sales, repair and maintenance services for customer-owned equipment.
- How these are delivered:
  - Manufacturing of frozen and baked products.
  - Distribution to foodservice and retail supermarket channels.
  - Installation and servicing of frozen beverage dispensers; provision and retention (company-owned placement) of merchandising/equipment at customer locations.
  - Sales through distributor network and company distribution for certain beverage brands.
- Primary customer type (B2B, B2C, government, mixed): Mixed — primarily B2B (foodservice operators, supermarket chains, distributors, institutions) with end-consumer sales via retail supermarkets and foodservice point of sale.

3. Revenue Drivers and Operating Segments
- Major operating segments (ranked by company reporting):
  1) Food Service
     - Description of activities: Sells soft pretzels, frozen novelties, churros, handheld products and bakery products to foodservice customers (snack bars, food stands, chain stores, malls, restaurants, stadiums, parks, theatres, schools, colleges, institutions).
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Not stated at segment level. Product-level shares reported (see below).
  2) Retail Supermarkets
     - Description of activities: Sells frozen and prepackaged products to retail supermarket chains (soft pretzels, frozen novelties, handheld products, whole fruit bars, Minute Maid products, Dogsters, Philly Swirl, Icee Squeeze Up tubes).
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Not stated at segment level.
  3) Frozen Beverages
     - Description of activities: Markets frozen carbonated and non-carbonated beverages (Icee, Slush Puppie, Parrot Ice) to foodservice in the U.S., Mexico and Canada; installs and services dispensers; supplies ingredients; provides repair/maintenance and sells equipment.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Frozen beverages sales were 15% of total revenue in fiscal 2024 (14% in 2023; 13% in 2022).
- Product-level revenue contributions (as stated):
  - Bakery products: 26% of sales (FY2024; 26% FY2023; 29% FY2022)
  - Soft pretzels: 18% of revenue (FY2024; 19% FY2023; 19% FY2022)
  - Frozen novelties: 17% (FY2024; 17% FY2023; 14% FY2022)
  - Frozen beverages: 15% (FY2024; 14% FY2023; 13% FY2022)
  - Churros: 7% (FY2024; 7% FY2023; 6% FY2022)
  - Handheld products: 7% (FY2024; 6% FY2023; 7% FY2022)
  - Equipment sales and repair/maintenance services: 9% (FY2024, FY2023, FY2022)

4. Industry and Market Context
- Industries the company explicitly states it operates in: Snack foods manufacturing; distribution/marketing of frozen beverages.
- End markets served: Foodservice (snack bars, food stands, chain and independent restaurants, department/discount/warehouse/club stores, convenience stores, malls, stadiums, theme parks, movie theatres, schools, colleges, institutions) and retail supermarkets (supermarket chains).
- Position in the value chain: Manufacturer and distributor of snack foods and frozen beverages; provider/installer of beverage dispensers and merchandising equipment; service provider for equipment repair and maintenance; private label and contract packer.

5. Geographic Footprint
- Primary geographic markets: United States (markets nationally to foodservice and retail supermarket industries).
- International operations (if any): Sells frozen beverages in Mexico and Canada; company has rights to market and distribute Icee and Slush Puppie in the continental United States and internationally (rights stated).

6. Assets, Infrastructure, and Capabilities
- Key physical assets relevant to operations:
  - Manufacturing equipment and facilities (manufacture and quick-freeze/packaging lines described).
  - Proprietary twister machines for shaping pretzels and other production equipment (e.g., extrusion/hand shaping, cryogenic freezing equipment for Dippin' Dots referenced).
  - Merchandising equipment supplied to customers (ovens, mobile merchandisers, display cases, warmers, proprietary combination warmer/display cases).
  - Frozen beverage dispensers (company-owned and customer-owned; company provides managed service/products to approximately 132,000 dispensers).
- Key non-physical assets (e.g., IP, software platforms, proprietary technology):
  - Proprietary formulas for soft pretzels and churros.
  - Trademarks/brand names and marketing rights (e.g., SuperPretzel, Dippin' Dots, Icee, Slush Puppie, Luigi's, Minute Maid-branded items).
  - Rights to market and distribute certain beverage brands (Icee, Slush Puppie).

7. Secondary or Ancillary Activities
- Additional business activities not central to revenue:
  - Equipment sales, repair and maintenance services for customer-owned equipment (9% of sales).
  - Supplying and retaining ownership of merchandising/equipment at customer locations (support to foodservice channel).
  - Private label and contract packing.
- Whether these activities are emerging, declining, or supportive (if stated): Not stated.

8. Recent Strategic Changes (if mentioned)
- Acquisitions, divestitures, restructurings, or material strategy shifts: Not stated

9. Revenue Concentration and Dependencies (if stated)
- Dependence on specific customers, industries, or contracts:
  - Top ten customers accounted for 45% (FY2024), 43% (FY2023), and 43% (FY2022) of sales.
  - Largest customer accounted for 9% of sales in FY2024 and FY2023, 8% in FY2022.
  - Several of the top ten customers are food distributors serving many end users.
  - Many customers do not enter into long-term contracts; customer purchase decisions based on price, product quality, consumer demand and service performance.
- Seasonal or cyclical characteristics: Not stated

10. Explicit Business Classification Signals
- Keywords or phrases the company uses to describe its business:
  - "manufactures snack foods", "distributes frozen beverages", "foodservice", "retail supermarket", "private label", "contract packing", "frozen carbonated beverage", "frozen non carbonated beverage", brand names (e.g., Icee, Slush Puppie, Dippin' Dots, SuperPretzel).
- NAICS, SIC, or other industry classifications mentioned (if any): Not stated

11. Exclusions and Clarifications
- Activities mentioned but explicitly stated as not core: Not stated
- Clarifications the company provides about what it does not primarily do: Not stated

END OF SUMMARY

    - Relative contribution to revenue: Primary (company operates as a single segment)
- Major end-market revenue drivers (not separate GAAP segments but identified markets):
  - Semiconductor equipment market — primary target market (plasma power, high-voltage, system power, sensing)

  - Data center computing market — high-efficiency, high-density server power conversion solutions
  - Telecom and networking market — application-specific AC-DC and DC-DC power conversion (customized/ruggedized solutions)

  - Wireless infrastructure and computer networking equipment

- Core products and/or services:
  - Branded home improvement and building products including: architectural coatings (paints, primers, stains, waterproofing), paint applicators/accessories; plumbing products (faucets, showerheads, valves, bath hardware, sinks, bathing units, shower enclosures, drains, steam shower systems, water filtration, connected water products); spas, exercise pools, aquatic fitness systems, saunas; cabinet/door/functional/decorative hardware and related products; custom thermoplastic solutions, extruded plastic profiles, specialized fabrications, and PEX tubing.

  - Primarily manufacture and distribute branded products; sell through retailers, distributors, wholesale channels and some consumer-direct channels.

  - Mixed (B2B and B2C): home center retailers, online retailers, mass merchandisers, wholesalers and distributors, independent specialty retailers, plumbers, building contractors, remodelers, homebuilders, and end consumers.

- Major operating segments (ranked by importance):
  1) Plumbing Products (primary)
     - Segment name: Plumbing Products
     - Description of activities: Design, manufacture and sourcing of faucets, showering products, valves, bath hardware, sinks, bathing units, shower bases/enclosures, shower drains, steam shower systems, water filtration systems, spas/exercise pools/saunas, brass/copper/composite plumbing components, connected water products, custom thermoplastic and PEX tubing. Products sold to home centers, online retailers, mass merchandisers, wholesalers, distributors, specialty retailers, plumbers, contractors, remodelers, homebuilders and consumers. Manufacturing primarily in North America, Europe and Asia; sourcing from Asia and other regions.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Primary (largest segment; decorative architectural is ~32% — see below).
  2) Decorative Architectural Products (secondary)
     - Segment name: Decorative Architectural Products
     - Description of activities: Architectural coatings (paints, primers, specialty coatings, stains, waterproofing), paint applicators and accessories, branded cabinet and door hardware, functional hardware, wall plates, hook products, outdoor living hardware, decorative bath hardware, shower accessories, mirrors, shower doors. Products sold primarily in North America (also South America) to DIY and professional customers through home center retailers and other retailers.
     - Relative contribution to revenue: Secondary; architectural coatings comprised approximately 32% of consolidated net sales in 2024, 2023 and 2022.

- Seasonality: Decorative Architectural Products segment is seasonal with stronger sales in second and third calendar quarters (peak repair and remodel season).

- Industries the company explicitly states it operates in:
  - Home improvement and building products; architectural coatings; plumbing and bath fixtures; spas and aquatic fitness equipment; decorative and functional hardware.
